title: The Year-End Review: Rethinking a Learning Plan
instructions: 项目原创模拟场景与数据，不是官方试卷。阅读文章后独立回答10题，再检查逐题依据。题目包含信息定位、论证范围、比较及推断；遇到词汇可用划词帮助，但使用帮助不算独立测评。语法先看规则，再做新语境练习。
passage:
A. For twelve months, Mei had followed a strict study plan. Every morning she reviewed fifty new words, listened to a podcast for thirty minutes, and wrote a short paragraph. She rarely missed a day. Yet when she took a practice test in November, her score had barely moved. 'I feel like I've been running on a treadmill,' she told her teacher, Mr. Chen. 'I'm working hard, but I'm not going anywhere.' This is a common experience among language learners: effort alone does not guarantee progress if the effort is not directed well. Mei had confused activity with achievement, and the result was frustration rather than improvement. Many learners believe that more hours and more words must lead to better results, but without feedback and review, hard work can simply repeat the same weaknesses. In Mei's case, the daily routine felt productive because it was busy, but it never forced her to notice what she was getting wrong.

B. Mr. Chen asked her to bring her study logs to their next lesson. Together, they looked at the data. Mei had studied for 320 days. She had learned over 2,000 words. But when Mr. Chen asked her to use ten of those words in a conversation, she could only use three correctly. 'You have collected a lot of bricks,' he said. 'But you haven't built many walls.' The problem was not effort. It was the way she organized her learning. She treated every word as equally important and never reviewed the ones she kept forgetting. In other words, her input was large but her retention was weak, and she had no system for turning passive knowledge into active use. The logs made this visible: plenty of contact with English, but little evidence that the language was becoming usable. This gap between knowing a word and being able to use it is one of the most common hidden problems in language study.

C. They decided to change the plan for the next year. First, Mei would focus on 'high-frequency errors' — mistakes she made again and again. She would keep a simple error log with three columns: the mistake, the correct form, and a short example. Second, she would review old words more often than new ones. Mr. Chen explained that forgetting is normal, and scheduled review is more effective than constant new input. Third, she would practice speaking in short, focused sessions — five minutes a day — instead of long, unfocused conversations. Finally, she would take a full practice test every six weeks to measure progress. Each of these changes addressed a specific weakness in her old routine, replacing quantity with structure and repetition with purpose. The plan was smaller than her old one, but every part of it had a clear job. Nothing in it was included just to fill time.

D. Mei was skeptical at first. 'Won't I fall behind if I stop learning new words?' she asked. Mr. Chen shook his head. 'You won't stop learning. You'll just learn differently. Depth beats width at your level.' He showed her a simple checklist for exam preparation: 1) Check your error log before each practice test. 2) Review ten old words for every five new ones. 3) Record yourself speaking for two minutes and listen for repeated mistakes. 4) Do one timed reading passage every week. 5) Sleep well the night before the test. The checklist was deliberately short, so that Mei could follow it consistently rather than abandon it after a few days. A short list, he explained, is easier to trust and easier to repeat. Long plans often look impressive, but they are also easier to give up on when life gets busy.

E. Mei followed the new plan for three months. She did not learn as many new words, but she used the old ones more confidently. Her error log grew to forty entries, and she reviewed it every Sunday. By February, her speaking had improved noticeably. 'I still make mistakes,' she said, 'but now I know which ones matter most.' Mr. Chen smiled. 'That's the goal. A good plan doesn't eliminate mistakes. It helps you see them clearly.' Her progress was not dramatic in numbers, but it was real in performance, which is what a test actually measures. She could now point to specific changes in her speaking, not just to hours spent studying. This shift — from counting time to noticing quality — was the most important change of all.

F. At the end of the three months, Mei wrote a short reflection. 'I used to think more was always better,' she wrote. 'Now I think better is better. I still have a long way to go, but at least I know which direction I'm walking.' Her experience shows that effective study is not about doing more, but about doing the right things in the right order. For Mei, the change was not a matter of working harder; it was a matter of working with clearer evidence and a better system. Her story also suggests that progress is often quiet at first: it appears in small corrections, in fewer repeated errors, and in the confidence to use what you already know.

questions.prompt: How many days had Mei studied in the first year?
questions.explanation: 文中明确提到“Mei had studied for 320 days.”，因此答案是320天。

questions.prompt: What did Mr. Chen compare Mei's vocabulary learning to?
options: Collecting bricks but not building walls
answers: Collecting bricks but not building walls
questions.explanation: 陈老师说“You have collected a lot of bricks... But you haven't built many walls.”，用砖和墙比喻她学了很多词但不会用。
questions.evidence: You have collected a lot of bricks,' he said. 'But you haven't built many walls.

questions.prompt: What distinction does the comparison between bricks and walls highlight?
options: Contact with many words can differ from being able to use them effectively.
Memorising words is entirely unnecessary for communication.
Reading is the only skill worth practising.
The number of study days directly determines active vocabulary.
answers: Contact with many words can differ from being able to use them effectively.
questions.explanation: 砖多却没建墙，强调词汇接触量与可用能力不同；并非否定记词，也不是把天数换算成掌握。
questions.evidence: In other words, her input was large but her retention was weak, and she had no system for turning passive knowledge into active use.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with ONE WORD from the passage: Mr. Chen suggested that scheduled ______ is more effective than constant new input.
questions.explanation: 文中说“scheduled review is more effective than constant new input”，因此填review。
questions.evidence: scheduled review is more effective than constant new input

questions.prompt: Which item is NOT on Mr. Chen's exam preparation checklist?
options: Review ten old words for every five new ones.
Record yourself speaking for two minutes.
Take a full practice test every day.
Sleep well the night before the test.
answers: Take a full practice test every day.
questions.explanation: D段清单要求每周做一篇限时阅读，没有每天做整套模拟题。C段另行提出每六周做一次完整模拟测试。因此 Take a full practice test every day 不在清单上。
questions.evidence: 2) Review ten old words for every five new ones. 3) Record yourself speaking for two minutes and listen for repeated mistakes. 4) Do one timed reading passage every week. 5) Sleep well the night before the test.

questions.prompt: How often did Mei review her error log?
questions.explanation: 文中提到“she reviewed it every Sunday”，因此是每周日复习。

questions.prompt: What does the phrase “at your level” restrict in the teacher's advice?
options: It links the recommendation to Mei's current needs rather than making it a universal rule for every learner.
It guarantees the same outcome for all learners using the same word ratio.
It means Mei should permanently stop learning new words.
It says that review alone can replace every other skill.
answers: It links the recommendation to Mei's current needs rather than making it a universal rule for every learner.
questions.explanation: at your level限定建议适用对象；结合她保持率弱的情况，不能推出所有人固定同一比例、永不学新词或只复习即可。
questions.evidence: Depth beats width at your level.

questions.prompt: True, False, or Not Given: Mei stopped learning new words completely after the new plan.
questions.explanation: D段清单仍要求每复习十个旧词学习五个新词，E段也说她学习的新词比以前少。这表示减少新词输入，而非完全停止，因此该说法是 False。
questions.evidence: 2) Review ten old words for every five new ones.

questions.prompt: Decide whether the statement agrees with the passage: At the reported three-month point, the error log contained more than forty entries.
questions.explanation: 原文明确说日志增长到forty entries，即四十条；more than forty表示超过四十，与给定数量冲突。不能因为原文没写“没有超过”就选Not Given。
questions.evidence: Her error log grew to forty entries, and she reviewed it every Sunday.

questions.prompt: Which claim about the new plan is supported by the outcome reported?
options: Mei could identify improvements in using language, although she still had further progress to make.
The passage reports that she achieved a specified official examination band.
Three months of this plan removed all of her recurring errors.
The plan established that every learner needs exactly the same amount of review.
answers: Mei could identify improvements in using language, although she still had further progress to make.
questions.explanation: 原文报告使用旧词更自信、能指出具体口语改善，同时承认还有很长路；没有具体官方分数、零错误或对所有人的固定配额证明。
questions.evidence: She could now point to specific changes in her speaking, not just to hours spent studying.

grammar.title: 复盘表达：过去完成、范围限定与数量准确性
grammar.explanation: 复盘要把时间、数量和证据范围写准确。had +过去分词突出早于另一过去事件的经历；明确过去时间用一般过去时。more than是严格大于，no more than为不超过，exactly表示恰好，不能互换。情态与限定语防止把个人改善扩大为保证结果。定语从句可指出要纠正的具体错误，基础的第三人称-s、不可数名词和动名词仍可作为个别薄弱点巩固。
grammar.example: She could now point to specific changes in her speaking, not just to hours spent studying.

questions.prompt: Emphasise the period before the November test: By the time she took that test, she ___ the old routine for months.
questions.explanation: 过去完成时had followed突出早于过去测试的持续经历；will为将来，has following和had follow形式错误。
questions.evidence: Emphasise the period before the November test: By the time she took that test, she had followed the old routine for months.

options: I have seen that movie last week.
I saw that movie last week.
I have saw that movie last week.
I seen that movie last week.
answers: I saw that movie last week.
questions.explanation: last week是明确的过去时间，应该用一般过去时saw，不能用现在完成时。
questions.evidence: I saw that movie last week.

options: He is interested in learn English.
He is interested in learning English.
He is interested to learning English.
answers: He is interested in learning English.
questions.explanation: be interested in后面接动名词，因此用learning。
questions.evidence: He is interested in learning English.

questions.prompt: The count is exactly forty, and has been checked. Which statement preserves that count?
options: The log contains more than forty entries.
The log contains fewer than forty entries.
The log contains at least fifty entries.
questions.explanation: exactly forty明确等于四十；more than为大于，fewer than为小于，at least fifty至少五十，都与已核实数量不符。
questions.evidence: The count is exactly forty, and has been checked. Which statement preserves that count?

questions.prompt: Introduce the specific errors she repeatedly makes: She reviews the errors ___ recur in her speech.
questions.explanation: 先行词errors是物，that在定语从句中作recur主语；what不能直接接既有先行词，whose后需所属名词，whom用于人且作宾语。
questions.evidence: Introduce the specific errors she repeatedly makes: She reviews the errors that recur in her speech.

questions.prompt: Report a limited possibility rather than guaranteeing an exam result: This change ___ improve her performance, but the next test is still needed.
questions.explanation: may准确保留待验证的可能；will certainly和must always过度保证，cannot possibly则排除可能，都不符合limited possibility。
questions.evidence: Report a limited possibility rather than guaranteeing an exam result: This change may improve her performance, but the next test is still needed.

options: He suggested to take a break.
questions.explanation: suggest后面接动名词，不接不定式，因此用taking。
information是不可数名词，没有复数形式，谓语动词用单数is。
